title: Extending an embedding into the function field of a smooth curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $C$ be a smooth connected $k$-curve of dimension one [def-sc-curves], with function field $k(C)$ [def-sc-function-field], and let $Y$ be an integral proper $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-scheme-over-base], with function field $k(Y)=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}$. For every $k$-embedding $\varphi:k(Y)\hookrightarrow k(C)$ [def-pc-field-extension], there exists a $k$-morphism $F:C\to Y$ such that $F(\eta_C)=\eta_Y$ and the local-ring map $F^*:k(Y)\to k(C)$ is exactly $\varphi$. More precisely, if $i_C:\operatorname{Spec}k(C)\to C$ and $i_Y:\operatorname{Spec}k(Y)\to Y$ are the generic-point morphisms [def-sc-generic-point], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], then
$$F\circ i_C=i_Y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi).$$
For every nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$, this composite factors through $V$ by the map associated with $A\hookrightarrow k(Y)\xrightarrow{\varphi}k(C)$; on generic stalks it sends $a/b$ to $\varphi(a)/\varphi(b)$. Properness of $C$ and smoothness or dimension one of $Y$ are not assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (curves-theorem-curves-rational-maps), third proof paragraph, converse construction; Morphisms Tag 0BX7 (morphisms-lemma-extend-across), applied at every point of the smooth connected curve. Extracts old steps 1, 6 and the extension part of step 7.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] to $C$. It is integral, its generic stalk is the field $k(C)$, and every other point $P$ is closed with DVR stalk of fraction field $k(C)$. Each stalk is a valuation ring: at $\eta_C$ every nonzero element already belongs to the field; at $P$, write $z=ut^n$ as in clause 3. If $n\geq0$, then $z\in\mathcal O_{C,P}$; if $n<0$, then $z^{-1}=u^{-1}t^{-n}\in\mathcal O_{C,P}$. Thus the valuation-stalk extension theorem applies to the source $C$.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (theorem-curves-rational-maps), converse construction in the third proof paragraph; Tag 0BXY (lemma-extend-over-dvr), source local-ring hypothesis.

proof.text: Put $h=i_Y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi):\operatorname{Spec}k(C)\to Y$. Contravariance of the affine spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the fact that $\varphi$ fixes $k$ make this a $k$-morphism. For any nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$, [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] gives $\eta_Y\in V$ and the injective germ map $j:A\hookrightarrow k(Y)=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. The generic-point morphism $i_Y$ is the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}\to Y$ of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] at $\eta_Y$; by its affine description it factors through $V$ as $\operatorname{Spec}(j)$. Hence $h$ factors through $V$ as $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi\circ j)$, since $\operatorname{Spec}(j)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi\circ j)$.

source.place: Tags 01RW (definition-function-field), 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions), with Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), generic affine localization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-valuation-stalk-proper-target-extension] with $X=C$ and with the $k$-morphism $h$ constructed in step 2. The source is integral and has valuation local rings by step 1; the target is proper over $k$ by hypothesis. It yields a $k$-morphism $F:C\to Y$ satisfying $F\circ i_C=h=i_Y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$. This is the required extension identity.

source.place: Tag 0BX7 (lemma-extend-across), generic-point extension specialized to the valuation local rings of the curve; the global extension is precisely the cited node.

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], the sole point of $\operatorname{Spec}k(C)$ maps under $i_C$ to $\eta_C$, under $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ to the sole point of $\operatorname{Spec}k(Y)$, and under $i_Y$ to $\eta_Y$. Evaluating the identity in step 3 therefore gives $F(\eta_C)=\eta_Y$. By clause (2) of the same node, on their generic stalks the canonical morphisms $i_C,i_Y$ induce identity maps, and by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] (with $Q=0$) the stalk map of $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ at its point is $\varphi$. Taking the stalk maps of that same identity consequently gives $F^*=\varphi$. Explicitly, on $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ as in step 2, the map on $A$ is $\varphi\circ j$; every generic germ is $j(a)/j(b)$ with $b\ne0$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], and its image is $\varphi(j(a))/\varphi(j(b))$ because a ring homomorphism preserves inverses. The denominator is nonzero since $j$ and $\varphi$ are injective. This proves every affine and generic-stalk clause.
